newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat falls on USDA grain forecasts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat falls on USDA grain forecasts.

text.p: Australian wheat futures fell on the Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) on Thursday in reaction to overnight USDA forecasts of increased world grain production, although the local decline was less than traders anticipated.
January 1997 fell by A$5.00 to A$177 a tonne, March fell by A$6.50 to A$177 and November fell by A$3.50 to A$170. A total of 31 trades went through.
"I am surprised that it wasn't lower," Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said of Thursday's SFE wheat market. "It was quite a responsible market today."
"It hit new lows (but) there was good buying support around A$175 a tonne," he said.
Twenty January put options, representing 1,000 tonnes of wheat, traded at a strike price of A$175 on an A$8 premium.
January ASW futures remained in a very well-defined downtrend, showing no signs of bottoming, Lindsay said.

Overnight, the USDA raised its estimate for the 1996/97 world grain crop to 1,820.43 million tonnes from 1,702.20 tonnes. The estimate for Australia's 1996/97 wheat crop was raised to 19.5 million tonnes from 17.5 million tonnes.
